title: UNIT 2: MEASUREMENTS AND SCIENTIFIC METHODS
notes:
✓ Chemistry is an experimental science that depends on accurate measurements.

→ Measurements require standard units, appropriate instruments, careful recording and proper treatment of uncertainty and error.

title: 2.1 Measurement
notes:
✓ Measurement → the process of comparing an unknown quantity with an accepted standard unit.

◆ A measurement consists of:
✓ Numerical value.
✓ Unit.

◆ Example: 25.0 mL.

title: 2.1.1 SI Units
notes:
✓ SI (International System of Units) → the standard system of measurement used in science.

◆ Common SI base units:
✓ Length → metre (m).
✓ Mass → kilogram (kg).
✓ Time → second (s).
✓ Temperature → kelvin (K).
✓ Amount of substance → mole (mol).

→ Other quantities are expressed using derived units.

title: 2.1.2 Derived Units
notes:
✓ Derived units → units obtained by combining SI base units mathematically.

◆ Examples:
✓ Area → m².
✓ Volume → m³.
✓ Speed → m/s.
✓ Density → kg/m³.
✓ Force → newton (N) = kg·m/s².

title: 2.1.3 SI Prefixes
notes:
✓ SI prefixes → represent powers of ten and make very large or very small quantities easier to express.

◆ Common prefixes:
✓ kilo (k) → 10³.
✓ centi (c) → 10⁻².
✓ milli (m) → 10⁻³.
✓ micro (μ) → 10⁻⁶.
✓ nano (n) → 10⁻⁹.

◆ Example:
1 km = 1000 m.

title: 2.1.4 Laboratory Equipment
notes:
✓ Laboratory equipment → used to measure, transfer, heat, mix and analyze substances.

◆ Examples:
✓ Balance → measures mass.
✓ Graduated cylinder → measures liquid volume.
✓ Burette → accurately delivers variable liquid volumes.
✓ Pipette → transfers a measured volume.
✓ Thermometer → measures temperature.
✓ Beaker → holds and mixes liquids.

title: 2.1.5 Accuracy
notes:
✓ Accuracy → how close a measured value is to the true or accepted value.

✓ High accuracy → measurement is close to the true value.

→ Accuracy is mainly affected by systematic errors such as incorrect calibration.

title: 2.1.6 Precision
notes:
✓ Precision → how close repeated measurements are to one another.

✓ High precision → repeated measurements give very similar values.

→ A measurement can be precise without being accurate.

title: 2.1.7 Accuracy vs Precision
notes:
◆ ACCURACY
✓ Closeness to the true value.

◆ PRECISION
✓ Closeness of repeated measurements to each other.

◆ REMEMBER
✓ Accuracy = correct.
✓ Precision = consistent.

title: 2.1.8 Calibration
notes:
✓ Calibration → the process of checking and adjusting a measuring instrument against a known standard.

◆ Purpose:
✓ Improve accuracy.
✓ Detect systematic errors.
✓ Ensure reliable measurements.

◆ Example → calibrating a balance using a known standard mass.

title: 2.1.9 Error
notes:
✓ Error → the difference between a measured value and the accepted or true value.

◆ Two common types:
✓ Systematic error → consistent error in one direction.
✓ Random error → unpredictable variation between measurements.

→ Errors cannot always be completely eliminated, but they can be reduced.

title: 2.1.10 Uncertainty
notes:
✓ Uncertainty → the estimated range within which the true value of a measurement is expected to lie.

◆ Example:
25.0 ± 0.1 mL

→ This means the measured value is approximately between 24.9 mL and 25.1 mL.

title: 2.1.11 Exact and Measured Numbers
notes:
✓ Exact numbers → have no uncertainty because they are known exactly.

◆ Examples:
✓ 12 eggs = exactly 12 eggs.
✓ 1 m = exactly 100 cm by definition.

✓ Measured numbers → are obtained experimentally and always contain some uncertainty.

◆ Example:
A balance reading of 25.43 g is a measured number.

title: 2.1.12 Significant Figures
notes:
✓ Significant figures → the digits in a measured value that carry meaningful information about its precision.

◆ Rules:
✓ Non-zero digits are significant.
✓ Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
✓ Leading zeros are not significant.
✓ Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.

◆ Examples:
0.00450 → 3 significant figures.
25.0 → 3 significant figures.

title: 2.1.13 Decimal Places
notes:
✓ Decimal places → the number of digits written after the decimal point.

◆ Examples:
✓ 5.2 → 1 decimal place.
✓ 5.20 → 2 decimal places.
✓ 5.200 → 3 decimal places.

→ Decimal places describe the position of the last written digit, while significant figures describe meaningful digits.

title: 2.1.14 Scientific Notation
notes:
✓ Scientific notation → expresses numbers as:
N × 10ⁿ

✓ N is between 1 and 10.

◆ Examples:
3000 = 3.0 × 10³.
0.00045 = 4.5 × 10⁻⁴.

→ It is useful for very large or very small measurements.

title: 2.2 Scientific Method
notes:
✓ Scientific method → a systematic approach used to investigate scientific questions.

◆ Main steps:
✓ Observation.
✓ Question or problem.
✓ Hypothesis.
✓ Experiment.
✓ Collection and analysis of data.
✓ Conclusion.
✓ Communication of results.

✓ A good hypothesis must be testable.

title: 2.2.1 Chemistry as Experimental Science
notes:
✓ Chemistry depends on experiments to test ideas and discover how substances behave.

◆ A scientific experiment should:
✓ Have a clear objective.
✓ Use appropriate equipment.
✓ Control relevant variables.
✓ Record observations and measurements.
✓ Analyze results.
✓ Draw a conclusion based on evidence.

title: 2.2.2 Laboratory Safety
notes:
✓ Laboratory safety → prevents accidents, injuries and contamination.

◆ Important rules:
✓ Wear appropriate protective equipment.
✓ Never taste chemicals.
✓ Do not directly smell chemicals; use safe wafting when instructed.
✓ Follow chemical labels and instructions.
✓ Keep the work area clean.
✓ Handle flames and glassware carefully.
✓ Report spills and accidents immediately.
✓ Dispose of chemicals properly.

title: UNIT 2 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
✓ Measurement → comparison with a standard unit.
✓ SI → international standard system of units.
✓ Derived unit → combination of base units.
✓ Calibration → checking an instrument against a known standard.

✓ Accuracy → closeness to true value.
✓ Precision → closeness of repeated measurements.
✓ Error → difference between measured and accepted value.
✓ Uncertainty → estimated range around a measurement.

✓ Exact number → no measurement uncertainty.
✓ Measured number → obtained experimentally and has uncertainty.

✓ Significant figures → meaningful digits in a measurement.
✓ Decimal places → digits after the decimal point.
✓ Scientific notation → N × 10ⁿ.

✓ Scientific method → observation → hypothesis → experiment → analysis → conclusion.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Accuracy = close to true value.
✓ Precision = close to each other.
✓ Calibration = checking the instrument.
✓ Uncertainty = range of possible values.
